newsitem.title: CANADA: February vote set on Canada Prairie barley issue.
newsitem.headline: February vote set on Canada Prairie barley issue.

text.p: Barley growers across the Canadian Prairies will vote in February on whether all types of Prairie-grown barley should be exported exclusively by the Canadian Wheat Board or by the private trade, Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said in a statement.
The farmer plebiscite will be administered by KPMG Chartered Accountants, the release stated.

The initial voter list will be based on CWB permit book information. Farmers without CWB permit books may be eligible by providing evidence they have grown barley in the last five years or by signing a legal affidavit to that effect.

Farmers will be asked to choose between exporting feed and malt barley throught private exporters or retain the status quo. Currently, all barley is exported through the CWB but domestic feed barley sales are handled privately.

"The contracting of an independent firm with the necessary expertise and professional credentials to oversee this vote is the most effective way to ensure an impartial and accurate process," Goodale said of the selection of KPMG.
Subsequent details on the voting process will be announced by KPMG's Winnipeg office in early January, Goodale said.
About 30 percent of barley grown on the Prairies is exported and the balance fed to livestock or brewed in Canada.
